title: Linearity is preserved and reflected by the etale abelian adjunction
statement: Let $U,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f:U\to V$ a morphism, and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $L$ be the inverse image on sheaves of sets, $a_S:L\dashv R$ its adjunction, $L_a$ the abelian inverse image and $a:L_a\dashv R_a$ its fixed adjunction, and $R_r$ the sectionwise direct image on ring sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. Write $F_{r,T}$ and $F_{a,T}$ for the forgetful functors to set sheaves on $T=U,V$. Fix a ring inverse-image functor $L_r$, an adjunction $a_r:L_r\dashv R_r$, and natural isomorphisms $e_r:L_rF_{r,U}\cong F_{r,V}L$ and $e_a:L_aF_{a,U}\cong F_{a,V}L$. Assume the two hom-equivalence equations: for every ring map $h:L_rG\to F$, $F_{r,V}(a_r(h))=a_S(e_{r,G}^{-1}\circ F_{r,U}(h))$, and for every abelian map $h:L_aG\to F$, $F_{a,V}(a(h))=a_S(e_{a,G}^{-1}\circ F_{a,U}(h))$. Sheaves of modules and their forgetful functors to abelian sheaves are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix any functor $L_M:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\mathrm{Mod}(L_r\mathcal O)$ and natural isomorphism $e:L_MF_U\cong F_VL_a$, and assume for every module $G$ the transported action equation just written out as follows: with $i_G=F_{a,U}(e_G)\circ e_{a,F_VG}$, the actual scalar multiplication morphisms satisfy $L(\mu_G)=i_G\circ\mu_{L_MG}\circ(e_{r,\mathcal O}^{-1}\times i_G^{-1})\circ\lambda$. Let $R_M$ be sectionwise direct image with scalars restricted along the ring unit $\mathcal O\to R_rL_r\mathcal O$. For every $G\in\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, $F\in\mathrm{Mod}(L_r\mathcal O)$ and abelian map $\alpha:L_aF_VG\to F_UF$, there exists a module map $h:L_MG\to F$ with $F_U(h)=\alpha\circ e_G$ if and only if there exists a module map $k:G\to R_MF$ with $F_V(k)=a(\alpha)$. This statement asserts only the linearity criterion, not a module adjunction.

proof.text: *Step 2 (the unit $\eta_G$ is $\mathcal O$-linear; Stacks 03D3, proof).* $\eta_G:G\to RLG$ is additive, being the abelian unit (notation above). Linearity is $\eta_G\circ\mu_G=\mu_{RLG}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O}\times\eta_G)$ with $\mu_{RLG}=R(L(\mu_G)\circ\lambda^{-1})\circ(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id})$. First, $R(\lambda)\circ\eta_{\mathcal O\times G}=\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\eta_G$ as maps $\mathcal O\times G\to R(L\mathcal O\times LG)=RL\mathcal O\times RLG$: composing with $\mathrm{pr}_i=R(\mathrm{pr}_i)$ gives $R(L\mathrm{pr}_i)\circ\eta_{\mathcal O\times G}=\eta\circ\mathrm{pr}_i$ by naturality of $\eta$. Then, by naturality of $\eta$ at $\mu_G$, $\eta_G\circ\mu_G=RL(\mu_G)\circ\eta_{\mathcal O\times G}=R(L(\mu_G)\circ\lambda^{-1})\circ R(\lambda)\circ\eta_{\mathcal O\times G}=R(L(\mu_G)\circ\lambda^{-1})\circ(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\eta_G)=\mu_{RLG}\circ(\mathrm{id}\times\eta_G)$. This is the commutative square of the source ($\mathcal O\times G\to f_*f^{-1}(\mathcal O\times G)\to f_*f^{-1}G$ against $\mathcal O\times G\to G\to f_*f^{-1}G$).

source.place: Lemma 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules), proof: the square showing the adjunction map G -> f_*f^{-1}G is O-linear

proof.text: *Step 3 (the counit $\varepsilon_F$ is $u^{-1}\mathcal O$-linear; omitted in the source, written here).* $\varepsilon_F:LRF\to F$ is additive, being the abelian counit. Linearity is $\varepsilon_F\circ L(\mu_{RF})\circ\lambda^{-1}=\mu_F\circ(\mathrm{id}_{L\mathcal O}\times\varepsilon_F)$, i.e. (composing with the isomorphism $\lambda$) $\varepsilon_F\circ L(\mu_{RF})=\mu_F\circ(\mathrm{id}\times\varepsilon_F)\circ\lambda$ as maps $L(\mathcal O\times RF)\to F$. By naturality of $\varepsilon$ at $\mu_F$, $\varepsilon_F\circ L(\mu_{RF})=\varepsilon_F\circ LR(\mu_F)\circ L(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id})=\mu_F\circ\varepsilon_{L\mathcal O\times F}\circ L(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id}_{RF})$. It remains to see $\varepsilon_{L\mathcal O\times F}\circ L(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id})=(\mathrm{id}\times\varepsilon_F)\circ\lambda$ as maps into the product $L\mathcal O\times F$, i.e. after each projection. First projection: by naturality of $\varepsilon$, $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varepsilon_{L\mathcal O\times F}=\varepsilon_{L\mathcal O}\circ LR(\mathrm{pr}_1)$, and $R(\mathrm{pr}_1)\circ(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id})=\eta_{\mathcal O}\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$, so the left side gives $\varepsilon_{L\mathcal O}\circ L(\eta_{\mathcal O})\circ L(\mathrm{pr}_1)=L(\mathrm{pr}_1)$ by the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{LX}\circ L(\eta_X)=\mathrm{id}$; the right side gives $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\lambda=L(\mathrm{pr}_1)$. Second projection: likewise $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\varepsilon_{L\mathcal O\times F}\circ L(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id})=\varepsilon_F\circ L(R(\mathrm{pr}_2)\circ(\eta_{\mathcal O}\times\mathrm{id}))=\varepsilon_F\circ L(\mathrm{pr}_2)$, and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ(\mathrm{id}\times\varepsilon_F)\circ\lambda=\varepsilon_F\circ\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\lambda=\varepsilon_F\circ L(\mathrm{pr}_2)$. Hence $\varepsilon_F$ is $L\mathcal O$-linear.

source.place: Lemma 03D3, proof (the implication 'beta linear => alpha linear' is omitted there; this step and step 4(ii) supply it, written by an agent)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the two implications).* Let $\alpha:LG\to F$ be a morphism of abelian sheaves and $\beta=R(\alpha)\circ\eta_G$ its abelian adjoint; then $\alpha=\varepsilon_F\circ L(\beta)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] (a Mathlib leaf). (i) (Stacks) If $\alpha$ is $L\mathcal O$-linear, $R(\alpha):RLG\to RF$ is $\mathcal O$-linear by sectionwise restriction of scalars along the ring unit and $\eta_G$ is $\mathcal O$-linear by step 2, so their composite $\beta$ is $\mathcal O$-linear (a composite of linear maps is linear). (ii) (omitted in the source) If $\beta:G\to RF$ is $\mathcal O$-linear, $L(\beta):LG\to LRF$ is $L\mathcal O$-linear by the transported-action hypothesis and functoriality of LM (the module structure of $LRF$ being the one of the transported-action hypothesis and functoriality of LM applied to the $\mathcal O$-module $RF$ of sectionwise restriction of scalars along the ring unit) and $\varepsilon_F$ is $L\mathcal O$-linear by step 3, so $\alpha=\varepsilon_F\circ L(\beta)$ is $L\mathcal O$-linear.

source.place: Lemma 03D3, proof ('suppose alpha is f^{-1}O-linear, then clearly f_*alpha is ... O-linear. Hence it suffices to prove that the adjunction map is O-linear'); (ii) written by an agent

proof.text: A module map gives the underlying abelian map satisfying the scalar identity, by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Conversely scalar compatibility of an abelian map defines its sectionwise linear maps and hence a module morphism. Conjugating by e gives precisely the left-hand existential lift condition; applying the fixed abelian adjunction gives the right-hand condition. The preceding two implications establish the equivalence.
